title: A Small History of Quiet
paras: At a museum [[seminar|seminar]] on hearing protection, the smallest object on the table attracts particular attention: a pair of cotton earplugs coated in [[wax|wax]]. Such simple devices became commercially available in the early twentieth century, although the idea of blocking unwanted sound was much older.

Ancient Greek literature describes sailors stopping their ears to escape dangerous singing. This is not a [[factual|factual]] account of medical practice, but it shows how early people imagined controlling what they heard. Modern earplugs developed through [[adaptation|adaptation]] to different conditions. Busy streets disturbed sleepers, while factory machinery exposed workers to noise that could permanently damage hearing.

Early soft plugs could be warmed between the fingers and shaped to fit the ear. Unlike a rigid object, they pressed gently against the skin. Nevertheless, an uncomfortable fit might make a wearer [[moan|moan]] rather than sleep. An [[illustration|illustration]] in a medical publication could explain correct placement, but printed advice did not guarantee careful use. With the growth of [[aerial|aerial]] warfare, protection from powerful engine noise also became increasingly important.

Museums now [[acquire|acquire]] old packets and instruction sheets to document this modest technology. Even a notice requesting [[renewal|renewal]] of a factory's medical-journal subscription can reveal how advice circulated. At the discussion table, disagreement is lively rather than [[aggressive|aggressive]]. One visitor asks whether providing earplugs could ever replace efforts to make the workplace itself quieter.
zh: 在博物馆一场关于听力保护的研讨会上，桌上最小的物件格外引人注意：一副涂蜡的棉质耳塞。这类简单装置在二十世纪初开始上市销售，不过，阻隔不受欢迎的声音这一想法，出现得要早得多。
古希腊文学描写过水手堵住耳朵，以躲避危险歌声的情景。这并不是对医疗实践的事实记录，却表明人们很早就设想过控制自己听到的声音。现代耳塞的发展，是不断适应不同环境的过程。繁忙的街道打扰人们睡眠，而工厂机器则让工人暴露在可能永久损伤听力的噪声中。
早期的软耳塞可以用手指捂暖，再捏成适合耳朵的形状。与硬物不同，它们只是轻轻贴压皮肤。然而，如果佩戴不适，使用者可能会难受得呻吟，而不是安然入睡。医学刊物中的插图可以说明正确的放置方法，但印在纸上的建议并不能保证人们会谨慎使用。随着空战的发展，防范发动机产生的强烈噪声也变得越来越重要。
如今，博物馆会收集旧包装和使用说明，以记录这项不起眼的技术。即便是一张要求工厂续订医学期刊的通知，也能揭示相关建议是如何传播的。在讨论桌旁，人们争论得热烈，却并不咄咄逼人。一位参观者问，提供耳塞是否有可能替代让工作场所本身变得更安静的努力。

q.s: The first commercially available earplugs were mainly bought by factory workers.
q.why: 首段未说明最早上市耳塞的主要购买者。

q.s: Ancient Greek literature includes an example of people blocking sound from their ears.
q.why: 第二段提到水手堵耳以躲避歌声。

q.s: Printed instructions ensured that people used earplugs carefully.
q.why: 第三段明确说印刷建议不能保证谨慎使用。
